concepts.def: An individual's ability to control information about themselves, challenged by large-scale data collection, tracking and profiling by software systems.
The monitoring of people's activities and communications using technology, raising tensions between security benefits and civil liberties.
Systematic unfairness in automated decisions, often arising when systems are trained or designed using data that reflects existing prejudices.
The replacement of routine human work by software and machines, displacing some jobs while creating new, often more technical, roles.
Laws such as UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 that regulate the processing of personal data and grant individuals enforceable rights.
The impacts of computing on the planet, including energy-hungry data centres, resource extraction for hardware, and growing e-waste.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Consequences Of Uses Of Computing — a core area of A-Level Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Consequences Of Uses Of Computing brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Consequences Of Uses Of Computing.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Algorithmic bias most commonly arises when:
options: A system is trained on data that reflects existing human prejudices
A computer overheats during processing
The screen brightness is set too high
Programs are written in older languages

mcqs.q: Creating or distributing malware to damage systems is criminalised in the UK by:
options: The Computer Misuse Act 1990
The Highways Act
The Consumer Rights Act
The Equality Act

mcqs.q: Which right do individuals have under UK data protection law?
options: To access the personal data organisations hold about them
To read anyone else's emails
To force any website to close
To copy any database they like

mcqs.q: A widely discussed consequence of large-scale automation is:
options: Displacement of routine jobs alongside the creation of new technical roles
The end of all electricity use
Slower computers everywhere
The disappearance of the internet

mcqs.q: Are decisions made by algorithms automatically neutral and objective?
options: Yes - bias is impossible once a process is automated.
No - algorithms inherit the assumptions of their designers and the biases in their training data, so they can systematically disadvantage groups of people.
Yes - automation has no effect on employment at all.
Yes - computers have no opinions, so their decisions are always fair.

mcqs.q: Does anonymising a dataset guarantee individuals can never be identified?
options: Yes - anonymised data is no longer data about people at all.
Yes - removing names makes re-identification impossible.
No - combining an anonymised dataset with other available data can often re-identify individuals, which is why anonymisation alone is not a complete safeguard.
Yes - automation has no effect on employment at all.
Yes - automation has no effect on employment at all.
Yes - bias is impossible once a process is automated.
No - automation displaces some roles while creating others, such as development, maintenance and data analysis; the effects are uneven across skills and regions.
Yes - every automated task is a job lost forever with nothing created.
